result.topic_en: Gauss expresses the arithmetic-geometric mean in terms of theta-type series, gives a formula for the nome x (with a Briggs-logarithm numerical example for the AGM of 3 and 1), notes the general form of all values of the AGM, and states a differential relation he calls a beautiful theorem.
result.transcription:
Math 27
(12) [-47a-] 12
Arithmetisch-geometrische Mittel.

$m = \mu(1+2x+2x^4+2x^9+\text{etc.})^2$
$n = \mu(1-2x+2x^4-2x^9+\text{etc.})^2$
$\sqrt{(mm-nn)} = \mu(2x^{\frac14}+2x^{\frac94}+2x^{\frac{25}{4}}+\text{etc.})^2$

Das AGMittel zwischen $m$ und $\sqrt{(mm-nn)}$ sei $=\lambda$. Man hat dann
$\lambda = \frac{\pi\mu}{\log\frac1x}$ oder $x = e^{-\frac{\pi\mu}{\lambda}}$.

Für Briggische Logarithmen wird $\lambda = \frac{a\mu}{\log\frac1x}$, wo $\log a = 0,1349342$ {+$= \log(\pi \log e)$[?]+}
Auch kann man sich folgender Formel bedienen:
$x = \frac{mm-nn}{16\, m' \cdot \sqrt{m''} \cdot \sqrt[4]{m'''} \cdot \sqrt[8]{m^{iv}} \,\&c.} = \frac{m-n}{8\sqrt{m''}\cdot\sqrt[4]{m'''}\,\sqrt[8]{m^{4}}}$

Die A.G. Mittel gestalten sich anders, wenn man für ein $n', n'', n'''$ &c. den negativen Werth wählt: doch sind alle Resultate in folgender Form begriffen:
$\frac{1}{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\mu} + \frac{4ik}{\lambda}$

Schöner Lehrsatz
$\frac{\frac{2\partial m}{m} - \frac{2\partial n}{n}}{mm-nn} = \frac{\frac{\pi\cdot\partial\lambda}{\lambda} - \frac{\pi\cdot\partial\mu}{\mu}}{\lambda\mu}$:

methods.what: Parametrization of m, n and sqrt(m^2-n^2) by squares of theta series in the nome x, with mu the AGM
Relation between the AGM of the complementary pair and the nome: x = exp(-pi mu/lambda)
Version of the formula for Briggs (base-10) logarithms
Infinite product formula for the nome x in terms of the successive AGM terms
Numerical computation of AGM(3,1) ≈ 1.8636167 and AGM(3, sqrt 8) ≈ 2.9135822 with logarithms, and computation of log x two ways
General form of all values of the multivalued AGM when negative roots are chosen
Differential relation between m, n and the AGMs mu, lambda

items.english: The A.G. means turn out differently if one chooses the negative value for one of n', n'', n''' etc.; yet all results are contained in the following form: 1/(mu) = 1/mu + 4ik/lambda
Beautiful theorem: (2dm/m - 2dn/n)/(mm-nn) = (pi dlambda/lambda - pi dmu/mu)/(lambda mu)
